summary: This article explains what makes a city a capital, how countries choose or build their capital cities, and examples from around the world, including Riyadh as the capital of Saudi Arabia.
introduce: Read the title “Capitals of the World” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: a large area or part of a country
important because of its connection to the past
carefully designed or arranged before being built or done

challengeTerms.def: having to do with managing or running an organization or government
to move something, such as an office or a capital, to a new place
representing something important beyond its ordinary, practical meaning

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a country's capital city should always be its largest city? Use evidence from the article to explain.
The article explains that some capitals are historic cities, while others are planned cities built for the role. Which kind of capital do you think works better for a country?
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review region, historic, and planned, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use administrative, relocate, and symbolic in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
